⚠ WINDOWS CASE-ONLY RENAME TRAP (measured phase 7, 2026-09-29). `fs.renameSync(from, to)` where only a *directory* component changes case and the filename is identical is a **silent no-op** on NTFS: `mkdirSync(dirname(to))` matches the existing dir case-insensitively, so source and destination resolve byte-identically and MoveFileEx treats it as a self-move. The codemod printed "moved importExport/commands -> importexport/commands" for all 40 paths and moved none of them — the import specifiers WERE rewritten, so the tree then said `./importexport/commands` while the directory on disk was `importExport/`, which works on Windows and breaks on any case-sensitive filesystem (CI/Linux/macOS). Fix: rename the *directory* two-step (via a temp name), and force the git index with `git update-index --force-remove <old>` + `git add <new>` because `git add -A` cannot see a case-only change when `core.ignorecase=true`. Note the shim blocks renaming a directory that contains subdirectories, so `importExport/` had to be rebuilt: create the target, move files in, remove the emptied old tree, rename into place.

✅ FIXED after phase 8 (2026-09-29): `kernel/eventBus.ts` imported `getWorkspaceSyncStatus` + `getWorkspaceGitState` from `gitops/` — two VALUES — which made §5.1's "kernel/ imports nothing engine-internal" false. `emitEntityStatus()` moved to `runtime/entityStatus.ts`, the engine's SECOND seam module (the first is `runtime/instances.ts`, §4.1). It could not move to `gitops/`: three of its four callers are `workspace/`-side (`workspace/entities/coreCommands.ts`, `workspace/entities/entityCrudCommands.ts`, `workspace/healthbarCommands.ts`) and §6 lets `workspace/` import only `kernel/` + `utils/`, so a sideways move would have turned 2 `kernel → gitops` edges into 3 `workspace → gitops` ones and changed nothing. `kernel/eventBus.ts` now has exactly ONE engine-internal import and it is a type (`WebhookPayload`). The ratchet's allowlist dropped 24 → 22 in the same commit, and its seam exemption is now a named SET (`SEAM_MODULES`) so a third seam module is a deliberate act.

✅ POST-PHASE-8 LAYOUT CLEANUP (2026-09-29) — the allowlist went 22 → 0, i.e. every violation the ratchet found is now fixed rather than excused. Four structural moves: (1) **`utils/` is pure again** — `utils/response.ts` → `proxy/response.ts` (it had exactly ONE importer; phase 4's 'both halves need it' was wrong), and `utils/server.ts` was split into `workspace/dispatch.ts` (EnabledSets, loadEnabledSets, activeEnv, workspaceCfg — these read enabled.json, so they are persistence), `utils/id.ts` (mkId) and `utils/net.ts` (hostnameOf). `sendHtml` was extracted DOWN from `reverseproxy/pages.ts` into `utils/sendHtml.ts`, which removed the last three `proxy → reverseproxy` edges. (2) **`gitops/gitStore.ts` → `workspace/gitStore.ts`** — it resolves paths via workspaceFs and holds a PER-WORKSPACE handle cache, and gitops/ imported workspace/ in seven files, so `workspace → gitops` was a CYCLE. One move fixed six violations. (3) **`blob/` → `workspace/blob/`** — a disk-backed content-addressed store with a TTL sweeper is persistence. (4) **`fileops/commands.ts` split** — the `tls.*` trio went to `certificates/certCommands.ts` (they resolve caCertPath/caKeyPath, that module's own constants) and `runner.exportReport` to `runner/runnerCommands.ts` (it renders through renderRunnerHtml, which `runner.saveReport` in that same file already calls). `fileops/` keeps `audit.export` + `capture.shareJson`. Three §6 rows were WIDENED, each for a stated reason: `transport/` gains `utils/` (the row predates the P15 WI2 extraction of utils/net.ts), `reverseproxy/` gains `proxy/` (the reverse half dispatches into the forward half's upstream machinery — ONE-WAY, so not a cycle), and that is it — `fileops`/`importexport` did NOT need a blob grant once blob moved under workspace/.
